title: JavaScript DOM Small Examples
description: Use these small JavaScript DOM examples with the tools described in each lesson. Read the expected result before you try a change.

examples.title: Find a page element
examples.description: The DOM gives JavaScript a way to work with the parts of a page.
examples.code: Reading club
examples.output: The heading stays on the page. The console shows Reading club.

examples.title: Change words safely
examples.description: textContent replaces the text inside an element.
examples.output: The paragraph changes from Waiting to Welcome, Mia!.

examples.title: Choose several elements
examples.description: querySelectorAll gives a list of all matches.
examples.output: The list shows Pack: Seeds and Pack: Water.

examples.title: Change a class
examples.description: classList changes class names on an element.
examples.output: The paragraph gets the bright class, so its background becomes gold.

examples.title: React to a click
examples.description: An event listener is a function that runs when an event happens.
examples.output: Clicking the button puts Hello, reader! in the paragraph.

examples.title: Read a form value
examples.description: An input value is the text currently typed into a field.
examples.output: Typing Mia and submitting shows Hi, Mia without loading a new page.

examples.title: Create a new element
examples.description: createElement makes a new page part. append puts that part inside an existing element.
examples.output: The empty list gains one item named Moon Trip.

examples.title: Remove a page part
examples.description: The remove method takes an element out of the page.
examples.code: This tip can be closed.
examples.output: The first click removes the tip. Later clicks do nothing because ?. checks that the tip still exists.

examples.title: Use one listener for a list
examples.description: Events often travel from a child to its parent.
examples.output: Clicking Choose shows Moon Trip. The listener lives on the parent div.

examples.title: Keep focus visible
examples.description: Focus marks the control that receives keyboard input.
examples.code:
<label for="search">Find a book</label><input id="search"><button id="start">Go to search</button>
<script>
  document.querySelector("#start").addEventListener("click", () => {
    document.querySelector("#search").focus();
  });
</script>
examples.output: Clicking Go to search moves focus into the search field. You can then type.

examples.title: Read an extra data value
examples.description: A data attribute stores a small extra value on an HTML element.
examples.code: Garden Days
examples.output: The console shows 45. Number changes the text 40 into a number before adding 5.

examples.title: Build a tiny counter
examples.description: A page can keep a number in JavaScript and show it in an element.
examples.code: Books read: 0
examples.output: Three clicks make the output show 3. Reloading this example starts again at zero.
